acceptanceCriteria: Scene lighting and environment are upgraded (dark gradient background, subtle fog, a soft ground/grid plane, environment lighting, and a contact shadow) without introducing decorative idle animation or expensive continuous per-frame effects.

Each element category has a materially distinct, semantically-motivated material treatment as specified (Work Item envelope translucent/glass, Runtime metal with a controlled emissive edge, Human-Computer Interaction neutral translucent surface, Knowledge a small luminous node graph, Repository heavy matte) rather than uniform boxes with only color differences.

The Work Item envelope's stage-to-stage change (start/checkpoint/finish/archive/close) is a smooth, bounded transition rather than an instant swap, and this transition respects prefers-reduced-motion by falling back to an instant change.
Active-flow data-pulse motion (introduced in WI-005) is visually refined (clear directionality, readable at a glance) without becoming a particle effect or bloom-heavy spectacle.
No Blender/GLB dependency or custom shader material is introduced; only Three.js/React Three Fiber/drei primitives and standard materials are used.

All previously-established acceptance behavior remains green -- camera stability (single focus settle, rapid multi-click, 5s idle stability), three navigation modes, full en/ja/zh-CN i18n coverage including 'Verified != Approved', the restrained default Overview screen, and the Work Item envelope / Knowledge / Traceability / HCI features from WI-005.

npm ci, lint, typecheck, unit tests, Playwright e2e, and the static export build all succeed, and no continuous unnecessary re-renders are introduced (idle scene stays visually still except for the deliberate active-flow pulse and any in-flight transition).
goal: Ship v0.2.2: improved scene lighting/environment (dark gradient background, faint fog, soft ground/grid, environment lighting, contact shadow), semantically-differentiated materials per element (Work Item envelope: translucent/glass; Runtime: metal + controlled emissive edge; Human-Computer Interaction: neutral translucent surface; Knowledge: small luminous graph; Repository: heavy matte), a smooth (not instant) Work Item envelope stage transition, and refined active-flow data-pulse motion -- all while staying greybox (no Blender, no custom shaders, no particle systems) and not regressing any established acceptance behavior from WI-001 through WI-005 (camera stability, three modes, i18n, Verified != Approved, restrained default screen).
intent: Upgrade the Explorer's spatial visual quality from a Three.js architecture prototype to a serious, restrained engineering instrument, now that the information architecture (Governance Loop, Work Item envelope, Knowledge, Traceability, HCI, per-flow activation) is in place from prior WIs.
outOfScope: Changing the Governance Loop information architecture
or i18n content established in prior WIs
Camera controller internals (WI-004 already fixed this; only new camera targets if truly needed)
